paper.title_en: Cooperativity-enhanced single-photon emission in a topological quantum emitter chain
paper.abstract_en: Single-photon emitters are one of the key elements in state-of-the art quantum technologies, yet optimizing and manipulating their emission requires precise fabrication of the emitter systems themselves. Here, we propose a route to tailored single-photon emission by exploiting cooperative effects in a topological single-photon emitter chain. Although the involvement of multiple emitters normally suppresses single-photon emission, we show that localized topological edge modes restore single-photon emission and protect against local perturbations. At the same time, cooperative effects occur due to the collective nature of the edge modes, leading to directional emission and linewidth narrowing. Our findings open new possibilities for tailoring single-photon emission by combining cooperativity and topological effects.
